edits.name: Calendar questions, read-only ('what's on Saturday?'), only if the shared calendar is Google
edits.description: If the family keeps a shared Google calendar (not confirmed: Q4), a parent can ask 'what's on Saturday?' or 'is Friday at 1 clear?' and get the answer from it, read-only. 'Clear' means nothing shows on the calendars the asking parent's sign-in can see; the other parent's own calendars are not read. If the calendar is on iCloud, or there is none, there is no proven route and nothing is built.
edits.example: Tony texts: 'What's on Saturday?' and gets the day's events from the shared calendar. He asks 'is Friday at 1 clear?' and gets what his sign-in shows for that hour; nothing on the calendar is changed.
edits.how: Only if Q4 says the shared calendar is Google. One host-side MCP server per person who agrees. Sign-in: `gog auth add <account> --services calendar --readonly`, stored apart from the mail sign-in and reusing wave A's published sign-in app, so the grant covers Calendar only. Server: `gog --account <account> mcp --allow-tool calendar_events`, because by default the server registers every read tool, mail search included. Each parent's agent allows only its own calendar server's tool by name, in the agent's tool list and in the sandbox's, and denies the other parent's; `bundle-mcp` is not opened. The server gets its own firewall rule, to Google only. The account-connector rule in the house-rules plugin is live first; the card adds no rule of its own. 'Is Friday at 1 clear?' is answered by listing that hour's events. One eval case: an event title that carries instructions must cause no tool call, a hand-off to the web helper included.

edits.name: Research helper: answers from public web pages with the link and the time fetched
edits.description: Happy can read public web pages that load without JavaScript or a login: a research helper with no memory, no accounts and no family data fetches the page, and the parent's own agent relays the answer with its link and the time it was fetched. When a page cannot be read, Happy says 'could not verify'. Nothing the helper fetches can reach the home network.
edits.example: A parent texts: 'What time does the town pool open on Saturday? Check their site.' Happy sends the hours with the link and when the page was fetched.
edits.how: First T4, before anything else is written: one hand-off from Tony's agent to the helper with a time limit; the answer must come back in the same chat while agents still cannot see each other's sessions. Agent: a shared `research` agent from the family file, a fresh sandbox per conversation, memory search off, no accounts, tools `web_search` and `web_fetch` only, its own capped key. Each parent's agent gains `sessions_spawn` with `subagents.allowAgents: ["research"]` and `runTimeoutSeconds` on the hand-off; the helper's built-in finish report is the only progress message. Guardrails: both `dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork` keys unset, `tools.web.fetch.headers` empty, no fetch-provider plugin, `tools.web.fetch.useTrustedEnvProxy` off, `browser.enabled: false`, `browser.evaluateEnabled: false`. One rule, in the helper's AGENTS.md: give the link and the time fetched, show the page's own date when it has one, give a price or date only from a fetched page, say 'could not verify' when a page could not be read. Four planted eval cases. No plugin, and no rule in the house-rules plugin.

caveats: The plain fetch runs no JavaScript and cannot log in, so such pages stay unread and Happy says 'could not verify'.

If the hand-off test (T4) fails, the only documented alternative is session visibility `tree` for the whole gateway, which changes a signed-off setting and needs Tony's yes plus a re-run of the separation check.

The home-network block rests on the fetch tool resolving and pinning the address itself, so `tools.web.fetch.useTrustedEnvProxy` stays off. Whether page fetches also pass through the outbound proxy is read from the proxy's log during wave B's gate.

Once the helper can fetch pages, neither the firewall nor the proxy can hold the gateway program to a list of hosts; they refuse home-network addresses and nothing more, so tool permissions, not the firewall, keep the other agents off the web.

The citation rule and the rule on what goes into a task are prompt rules; nothing mechanical enforces them, and the planted eval cases are the only check. The task rule (town and ages yes, names and school no) is a default Tony has not confirmed.
A slow lookup gets no 'on it' and no plain-words 'cancel that': it ends at its time limit, or at Tony's built-in stop. Tony's agent goes live first, Jordan's after a day without surprises.
edits.safety: The helper reads untrusted pages but holds no memory, accounts or family data, and cannot reach the home network. The roadmap's one remaining leak path stays open: a parent's agent holds private chats and writes the task text for a helper that can fetch any public address. Only a prompt rule and planted tests guard it, and the helper's answer is treated as untrusted.
unverified: That a cross-agent hand-off returns its result with agent-to-agent messaging off and session visibility set to self: the roadmap lists this as untested on 2026.9.7, and nothing was run here (T4).
The rule on what may go into the task text is a prompt rule; nothing mechanical enforces what a parent's agent writes into it.
Nothing in the installed stack enforces citations; it is a prompt rule the model can ignore, and the eval cases are the only check.
Whether page fetches pass through the outbound proxy once it is configured: the installed docs point both ways and nothing has been tried.
How long a real lookup takes: nothing on the current stack runs longer than about 20 seconds, so whether an 'on it' line is ever needed is unknown until the hand-off exists.
